what: Kontoor Brands owns Wrangler and Lee jeans, spun out of VF Corporation in 2019, and in 2025 bought Helly Hansen, the Norwegian outdoor and workwear brand.
customers: Retailers such as Walmart, Target and department stores, and consumers buying through its own websites.
money: Western and everyday denim and apparel.
moat: Two century-old denim brands with strong recognition, and efficient supply chains.
risks: Debt of $1.3B after buying Helly Hansen.
Tariffs on imported apparel raise costs.
Dependence on a few large retailers.
opportunities: Revenue rose to $3.45B over the last twelve months with Helly Hansen.
Free cash flow of about $400M a year.
The forward P/E of about 13 is low if the acquisition delivers.
watch: Helly Hansen growth and Wrangler margins.
view: Kontoor is a cash-generating apparel company that used its cash flow to buy Helly Hansen, adding a growing outdoor brand to two mature denim brands. Free cash flow of about $400 million a year supports both the dividend and debt repayment.
The trailing P/E of 29 is inflated by deal costs; on forward estimates it is about 13. The market doubts that the acquisition will lift growth and worries about tariffs on imported clothing.
This turns on Helly Hansen. If it grows as management hopes, the shares look cheap. I think the price is reasonable with a decent dividend, but apparel is a tough business.
bull: Helly Hansen grows strongly, debt falls and earnings rise.
bear: Tariffs and weak retail demand squeeze margins while debt stays high.
